device_identity_resolution.detail: resolve_short_addr_for_device_id_hex() on ServiceRuntimeApi/ServiceRuntime is a string-in/string-typed-enum-out API purpose-built so web_ui never needs to parse or hold a core::DeviceId itself. It distinguishes 4 outcomes (kResolved/kMalformedHex/kUnknownDevice/kNoCurrentLocator) by checking CoreState.devices for identity existence before consulting DeviceLocatorRegistry for locator freshness -- these map 1:1 to the golden matrix's invalid_request(400)/device_not_found(404)/device_offline(409) distinction. Tested directly via the device delete/power/reporting routes' malformed-hex, unknown-device and offline-device paths in both test files.

uri_path_parsing.detail: extract_uri_device_id_hex() and extract_uri_device_id_and_reporting_segments() (web_v1_common.cpp) are the first URI path-segment parsers in this codebase, implemented with manual strncmp/strtoul pointer arithmetic (no sscanf, matching established convention). The host httpd_req_t shim gained a uri field (previously absent -- no pre-v1 handler needed one) and the httpd_method_t shim gained HTTP_PUT/HTTP_PATCH/HTTP_DELETE (previously only HTTP_GET/HTTP_POST existed). Tested via well-formed, malformed, and missing-suffix URIs across the device delete/power/reporting routes.

Every route's success path and every reachable golden-matrix error path (400 invalid_request, 404 device_not_found, 409 device_offline/conflict, 503 no_capacity) is asserted.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Unchanged from the GET-only pass's finding: OperationResultStore tracks network/config/OTA/RCP results as four separate typed result queues, each with its own take_*_result() method, sharing only a global request_id counter. A generic poll endpoint needs a discriminated union or a try-each-domain caller, neither of which exists; designing one is a distinct unit of work from the route-by-route mutation work this pass did.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: Every route this pass added that produces a pollable id (join-window, power, delete, network scan/connect, OTA/RCP) already returns that id in its 202 response body, so the poll route is purely additive once built -- nothing added in this pass needs to change to support it.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: Plan #6 (bundled Web UI migrated atomically to v1 routes and DeviceId) remains unimplemented, even though all the mutation routes app.js would need (power, join, remove, reporting) now exist.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Migrating app.js is a UI-layer change orthogonal to the backend contract work this pass scoped itself to, and plan #29 keeps S4 out of the production registration path the migrated UI would need to actually reach these routes at runtime -- migrating the UI to call routes that are provably unreachable in production would not be a meaningful atomic migration yet.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: assets/app.js is untouched and continues to use only legacy routes.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: OTA/RCP submit-failure error mapping (map_ota_submit_error_v1/map_rcp_submit_error_v1) collapses roughly ten domain-specific OtaSubmitStatus/RcpUpdateSubmitStatus failure reasons (manifest/board/project/schema/signature mismatches) into a single 400 invalid_request token, rather than adding a fine-grained ApiV1ErrorCode per reason.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: The plan's own 'golden matrix' concept (required change #4/#9) implies a small, stable top-level vocabulary; expanding it by ~10 codes to mirror every internal validation branch would work against that intent. Only kBusy (and, for RCP, kConflict) is distinguished, since 409 conflict vs 400 invalid_request is a genuinely different client-facing category (retry-later vs fix-the-request).
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: Clients cannot distinguish e.g. 'bad signature' from 'bad board' purely from the v1 error token; both are 400 invalid_request. The underlying detail is still available via server logs. This is a deliberate scope decision, not an oversight, and can be revisited without breaking the matrix's shape if finer granularity is wanted later.
